options.text: A generic open source automation framework for acceptance testing
A proprietary testing tool only for web applications
options.explanation: Robot Framework is open source, not proprietary, and can test more than just web applications

options.text: A programming language for test automation
options.explanation: Robot Framework is a framework, not a programming language itself

options.text: A tool specifically designed only for mobile testing
options.explanation: Robot Framework is generic and can be used for various types of testing, not just mobile

questions.question: Which of the following are key features of Robot Framework? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Robot Framework supports libraries written in Python, Java, and other languages
Robot Framework tests are interpreted, not compiled

questions.question: What are the two main use cases of Robot Framework?

options.explanation: Robot Framework is typically not used for unit or low-level integration testing

options.text: Test automation and robotic process automation (RPA)

options.explanation: While possible with extensions, these are not the main use cases of Robot Framework
Robot Framework is not designed for code compilation or deployment tasks

questions.question: Which of the following test levels is Robot Framework PRIMARILY used for? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Robot Framework is typically not used for component/unit testing due to its high-level abstraction
Low-level integration testing is not Robot Framework's primary strength

questions.question: Why is Robot Framework typically NOT used for component testing?

options.explanation: Robot Framework has excellent support for Python libraries
Robot Framework is specifically designed for automated testing

options.text: Component testing requires low-level, granular tests with direct code interaction, which is better handled by unit testing frameworks
Robot Framework is too fast for component testing
options.explanation: Speed is not the reason; the abstraction level and design philosophy are

questions.question: Which of the following is a common RPA use case for Robot Framework?

options.explanation: Code compilation is not an RPA task and not what Robot Framework is designed for

options.text: Data extraction and manipulation between systems

options.explanation: Kernel development is low-level programming, not an RPA task
Driver installation is a system-level task, not typical RPA

questions.question: What is the primary goal of Synthetic Monitoring (Active/Proactive Monitoring) in Robot Framework?

options.text: To monitor system resources like CPU and memory
options.explanation: Resource monitoring is infrastructure monitoring, not synthetic monitoring

options.text: To detect performance issues or downtime before they affect actual users

options.explanation: Code complexity analysis is static code analysis, not synthetic monitoring
Documentation generation is not related to synthetic monitoring
